doc.title: Vince Lateano interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Audio clip of the Cal Tjader band at the Catamaran in San Diego, Clare Fischer
summary: Shown a San Diego video clip, he recalls joining Cal in May 1978 and the Catamaran gig with Clare Fischer.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: I actually have a piece of music to play here, and I suppose this could be like a blindfold test, but I wouldn’t do that to you.
[audio interlude]
This is actually you. I think it’s you.
Yeah. I recognize that. That’s like sort of a bossa groove. [scats]
This is from a video in San Diego.
Yeah. I was with the band a month.
You were just with them a month?

Yeah I had just started with the band. That was ’78. I joined Cal I guess around May of ’78. And Clare Fischer, and Poncho, Rob Fisher, myself and Cal, and there was a great gig in San Diego, a place called the Catamaran in Mission Bay. It was like a musician’s dream kind of gig, where you go and you’re in a hotel sort of right on the water, it’s a thing you fantasize about. And you come down the elevator and you go into the club and play.
And then on breaks you can go back up to your room.

Exactly, exactly. And it’s just a kind of a great scene, yeah. And I did that quite a few times with Cal. And while we were there we went out to the college I think is where we did that, we went to a college, San Diego State or something like that. And they had a little studio and they had a sort of a mock nightclub, they had a few tables around where the camera could pick it up, and people sitting like at a club. And what I remember about that date was that they had me on a riser and there wasn’t room for my floor tom, so I had — which was fine, I mean, you know, you don’t need a lot of drums to get away with it. But it was like I kept trying to figure out how to move the drums — no I guess not, the hell with it. It’s not going to happen.
I guess the percussionist will play a little more tonight.
Yeah. But that was a great experience, having played with those musicians. Because it rubs off. You’re around them and —
I didn’t know that was Clare Fischer in that, playing the Fender Rhodes.
Yeah he didn’t like to play the piano. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
Really?
Well he said there weren’t any good pianos.
Yeah okay. He didn’t know what he was going to be playing?
Did you ever talk to Clare?
No.
Oh you’ve got to talk to Clare.
I’d love to, maybe you can — is he in L.A.?
Yeah. Studio City, yeah. He’s a brilliant musician/composer. I’ll leave it right there.
Okay. I can read between the lines that that would be interesting.
Oh very.
